name: Harley Whiskey Barrel Aged (SCA 87+)
description: Grown at elevation of 1050 MASL in the Sakleshpur region of Karnataka, these washed coffee’s from Harley Estate undergo a barrel ageing process in single malt whiskey barrels sourced from Amrut Distillers. This produces a cup which is fruity, boozy and sweet with notes of irish cream, green apple, stone fruit and hints of spice. The coffee is roasted to a medium level to increase the sweetness and balance the body & mallic acidity of the coffee. This coffee is suitable for espresso, pourover, aeropress and French press.

name: 4th Birthday Blend
description:
Rossette 4th Birthday Blend

Celebrate 4 years with a cup that tastes like party: a warm, indulgent blend made from two microlots from Ratnagiri Estate,that opens with tiramisu-soaked cocoa and rounded hazelnut, drifts into soft vanilla sweetness, and finishes with a playful rum-ball warmth. It’s our cake in a cup: familiar, celebratory, and crafted for every ritual that made Rossette what it is today.

name: Attikan Shade Barrel Fermented Washed
description:
One of our favourite estates to work with, Attikan brings us another standout lot this season. Nestled in the Biligiriranga Hills of Karnataka and run by the Sangameshwar Group, Attikan has long been a source of expressive, high-quality coffees that we’re always excited to roast. This year’s release is a 22-hour shade barrel fermented washed coffee, roasted by Rossette as a medium roast to bring out both complexity and balance.

In the cup, expect layered notes of plum, black grapes, prune, molasses, and milk chocolate. It’s a beautifully structured single-origin Arabica that shines equally well as a black coffee and with milk, where its sweetness and milk chocolate character come forward even more clearly. With medium acidity and a rich, smooth profile, this is a coffee that feels both elegant and comforting.

Whether you brew it as espresso, moka pot, AeroPress, or cold brew, Attikan is a must-try for anyone who loves sweet, fruit-forward coffees with depth and character.

name: Gungegiri Dark Honey
description:
We are thrilled to introduce the highly anticipated Gungegiri Dark Honey Coffee, a single-origin specialty from the renowned Gungegiri Estate in Chikmaglur, India. Grown at an elevation of 4,600 feet. Dark Honey processing leaves a generous amount of sticky, fruit-rich mucilage on the coffee bean during drying. This slow, shade-dried approach allows natural fruit sugars to deeply ferment and absorb into the seed, resulting in an exceptionally full-bodied cup with a heavy, viscous mouthfeel.

The coffee is a symphony of flavour that draws you in with its rich, dessert-like profile, reminiscent of a warm slice of banana bread enfolded with the sweetness of jaggery. The coffee's vibrant essence  of clementine and a subtle whisper of kiwi like finish

name: Yelnoorkhan Yeast Anaerobic Honey (SCA 85+)
description: Yelnoorkhan Anaerobic Honey coffee is produced using a method that combines anaerobic fermentation with honey processing. In this process, the coffee cherries are fermented in an oxygen-free environment, which enhances their fruity acidity and aromatic complexity. Following this, the beans are pulped and dried with some of the sticky mucilage (the 'honey') still attached, further enriching the coffee's sweetness and body. The resulting brew is lauded for its vibrant, grapes-like brightness, layered fruit notes, and a rich, raisin-like sweetness. These characteristics create a smooth and rounded mouthfeel, highlighting both the precision of controlled fermentation and the inherent qualities of the coffee's origin. This coffee is roasted to a medium-light level which allows us to brew it for both manual brews and complex espressos.

name: Hardoor Estate (Farm Organic) Washed

Produced by Mukul using his innovative 16-hour dry fermented washed process, this lot develops its signature high sweetness, impressively low acidity, and smooth medium body, revealing beautiful tasting notes of raisin, grapes, brown sugar, and floral honey that dance sweetly across the palate. Whether you're enjoying it as a comforting milk-based drink like a latte or cappuccino, or savouring it black as a clean Americano, this versatile coffee from Coorg's renowned estate delivers an elevated experience perfect for specialty coffee lovers seeking quality, complexity, and everyday indulgence. Ideal for all brewing methods

name: Colombian Huila Decaf
description:
Our first decaf, and it’s anything but boring. This coffee comes from San Agustín, Huila, grown at 1900 MASL, where the cool altitude brings depth and sweetness to every bean.

It’s washed processed, then decaffeinated using the DCM method : a gentle extraction that keeps the flavour, loses the caffeine.

Roasted medium-dark for espresso, this cup hits like a cozy dessert :Valencia Orange zest, roasted hazelnuts, and chocolate spread all rolled into one smooth finish. Perfect for your espresso machine, moka pot, AeroPress, or French press.

All the taste. None of the jitters.

name: 1615 West Giri (Light-Med)
description:
#1 SERIES - FRUIT FORWARD LOTS | 1615

Dense & juicy, balancing fruit clarity with tactile sweetness.

Suitable for all brew methods. Light Roast Indian Arabica Coffee.

Origin Krishnagiri Estate, West Giri Hills, Chikmagalur, Karnataka
Process A blend of single origin high grown arabica.
Varietal & Altitude
Chandragiri grown at high altitude.
Dry Aroma Red Berries & Jackfruit
Wet Aroma
Red Apples & Orange
Sensory Evaluation

Fresh watermelon, orange liqueur and a tea-like hibiscus finish.
Roast Profile
Light-Med Roast with low air flow, stable burner & higher development.
Characteristics


Fruit-forward & expressive with a dense, syrupy texture and rounded body.
Minimum resting period Filter 7 Days | Espresso 12 Days
A song that pairs well

 

About the region / estate :

By Producers Himu and Karunya, the estate is about the ancient land, its thriving ecosystem and our ability to work and interact within this complex structure of micro and macro organisms. It is about the coffee that is nurtured by this ecosystem and thrives only because every single organism (including humans) plays a conscious and balanced role. 

Krishnagiri Coffee is beyond the pale understanding of social media, it is an ineffable feeling that can only be understood by experiencing the land and its ecosystem. It is more than just Coffee! As for us, we are playing our small part in safeguarding the future of this land while finding innovative and sustainable ways to craft a perfect cup of Indian Coffee.

Roasters thought :

1615 was built around the idea of elevation.

The West Giri Hills rise to approximately 1,615 metres above sea level, a point where cooler temperatures and slower cherry maturation contribute to greater complexity and sweetness in the final cup. Rather than highlighting a single lot, we chose to assemble a blend of complementary high-grown coffees from the estate to capture a broader expression of the region.

The roast profile follows a light-medium approach with restrained airflow, stable energy application, and extended development. This allows the coffee to build density and sweetness without sacrificing the fruit character that defines the blend.

Our objective was to create a coffee that feels expansive rather than intense. The resulting cup opens with vibrant fruit notes reminiscent of watermelon and orange liqueur before settling into a softer floral finish. As the coffee cools, the sweetness becomes increasingly pronounced, revealing a layered structure that remains clean and balanced throughout.

1615 is our interpretation of the West Giri Hills, expressed through altitude, landscape, and season rather than any single process or variety.

Brew Approach:

18 GMS Med-Fine (Fellow Ode Gen 2.0, 3.8 Setting)
50 ML bloom 45 seconds 
Swirl immediately after pour
Then 80 ML
Then At 1.30 again 80 ML
Then again 80 ML to finish it off with gentle swirl in the end.

Water at 94° Celsius (TDS not more than 140 PPM).

For more brightness (lime forward)
→ go slightly coarser + reduce final pour agitation

For more sweetness (jaggery heavy)
→ grind finer + extend brew closer to 3 Minutes

name: Shevaroys Washed (Light-Med Roast)
description:
#1 SERIES - FRUIT FORWARD LOT | SHEVAROYS WASHED

Ripe tropical fruit notes of plums & Green Grapes.

Suitable for all brew methods. Ideal as Filter.

Indian Arabica Coffee with Tropical Fruity Sweetness.

Serving as Pourover at Bandra, Mumbai & Koregaon Park, Pune
Origin PKC Kudiraipanjan Estate, Shevaroys hills, Tamil Nadu
Process Mechanically washed with fresh stream water and soaked again for 48 hours then dried for 18 days, hulled and polished.
BRIX 24
Varietal & Altitude SLN 9 & Catimor grown at 1400 MSL
Dry Aroma Berries & Plums
Wet Aroma Plum, Figs & Grapes
Based on Sensory Evaluation

Ripe tropical fruit notes of plums & Green Grapes along with Pomegranates & cacao nibs finish.
Roast Profile Light-med Roast with variable drum speed and airflow with total roast time of 9 minutes.
Characteristics

Clean crisp profile with bright Acidity & Med-heavy body.
Minimum resting period Filter 5 Days | Espresso 21 Days
A song that pairs well

 

Roaster's thought :

The Shevaroys Washed opens our 1 Series with clarity and structure. Built to highlight origin character, this lot from PKC Kudiraipanjan Estate in the Shevaroys Hills of Tamil Nadu showcases the expressive side of high grown washed Arabica.

Grown at 1400 MSL with SLN 9 and Catimor varieties and harvested at 24.8 Brix, the cherries were mechanically washed using fresh stream water, soaked for 48 hours, and dried slowly over 18 days before hulling and polishing. The extended soak sharpens clarity while maintaining fruit integrity.

Roasted light to medium with controlled airflow and a total roast time of 9 minutes, this profile is designed to preserve acidity and aromatic lift while building structure.

In the cup, expect green kiwi, ripe grapes and raw honey, layered with plum and pomegranate brightness. A spearmint lift and cacao nib finish add dimension. The acidity is bright but refined, supported by a clean, crisp structure and a medium heavy body.

Roast Profile:

Sample Roast Machine : Bullet IBTS R1
Roast Machine : Probat VFD

Development % : 14
First Crack Temperature : Below 195° Celsius

Roast Time : 8.30 Minutes

Brew Approach:

18 GMS Med-Fine (Fellow Ode Gen 2.0, 3.8 Setting)
40 ML bloom 45 seconds 
Swirl immediately after pour
Then 80 ML
Then At 1.30 again 80 ML
Then again 80 ML to finish it off with gentle swirl in the end.

Water above 94° Celsius (TDS not more than 140 PPM).

Indian Arabica Coffee with Tropical Fruity Sweetness. Serving as Pourover at Bandra, Mumbai & Koregaon Park, Pune Origin PKC Kudiraipanjan Estate, Shevaroys hills, Tamil Nadu Process Mechanically washed with fresh stream water and soaked again for 48 hours then dried for 18 days, hulled and polished. BRIX 24 Varietal & Altitude SLN 9 & Catimor grown at 1400 MSL Dry Aroma Berries & Plums Wet Aroma Plum, Figs & Grapes Based on Sensory Evaluation Ripe tropical fruit notes of plums & Green Grapes along with Pomegranates & cacao nibs finish. Roast Profile Light-med Roast with variable drum speed and airflow with total roast time of 9 minutes. Characteristics Clean crisp profile with bright Acidity & Med-heavy body. Minimum resting period Filter 5 Days | Espresso 21 Days A song that pairs well Roaster's thought : The Shevaroys Washed opens our 1 Series with clarity and structure. Built to highlight origin character, this lot from PKC Kudiraipanjan Estate in the Shevaroys Hills of Tamil Nadu showcases the expressive side of high grown washed Arabica. Grown at 1400 MSL with SLN 9 and Catimor varieties and harvested at 24.8 Brix, the cherries were mechanically washed using fresh stream water, soaked for 48 hours, and dried slowly over 18 days before hulling and polishing. The extended soak sharpens clarity while maintaining fruit integrity. Roasted light to medium with controlled airflow and a total roast time of 9 minutes, this profile is designed to preserve acidity and aromatic lift while building structure. In the cup, expect green kiwi, ripe grapes and raw honey, layered with plum and pomegranate brightness. A spearmint lift and cacao nib finish add dimension. The acidity is bright but refined, supported by a clean, crisp structure and a medium heavy body. Water above 94 ° Celsius (TDS not more than 140 PPM).

name: THE YELLOW LOT
description:
#2 SERIES - ROASTERS ART | THE YELLOW LOT

Deeply sweet cup, Crema Rich & Heavy Bodied with Lingering aftertaste.

Suitable for all brew methods. Ideal as Espresso & Cold Brew.

Sweet & Dense Indian Arabica Coffee.

Origin Ratnagiri Estate, Chikmagalur
Process Anaerobic Fermented Naturals are hot washed followed by a rapid cold wash & eventually tumble mechanical dried at the farm.
BRIX 24.8
Varietal & Altitude SL9 grown at 4450 Feet
Dry Aroma Ripe Red berries
Wet Aroma Jackfruit, Dates & milk chocolate.
Based on Sensory Evaluation

Banana, Deep Date Sweetness along with milk chocolate and subtropical fruit finish.

Roast Profile Roasted above medium with high DTR & variable drum speed.
Characteristics

Deeply sweet cup, Crema Rich & Heavy Bodied with Lingering aftertaste & balanced acidity.
Minimum resting period Filter 7 Days | Espresso 11 Days
A song that pairs well

 

Roaster's thought :

Sourced from Ratnagiri Estate in Chikmagalur, this SL9 lot was grown at 4450 ft and harvested at a Brix of 24.8, allowing for deep sugar development before processing. The coffee undergoes anaerobic fermentation, followed by a hot wash and rapid cold wash, then tumble mechanical drying at the estate to stabilise the fruit intensity.

Roasted above medium with a high development ratio and variable drum speed, this profile is designed to push sugar caramelisation while preserving the fruit core.

In the cup, expect ripe banana, deep date sweetness and milk chocolate layered over a subtle melon finish. The body is heavy and syrup like, producing a dense crema and a long, structured aftertaste with balanced acidity.

Versatile across brew methods, it performs exceptionally well in milk, where the sweetness expands and the texture becomes velvety and round.

Roast Profile:

Sample Roast Machine : Bullet IBTS R1
Roast Machine : Probat VFD

Development % : 17
First Crack Temperature : Below 195° Celsius 

Brew Approach:

19 GMS Med-Fine (Fellow Ode Gen 2.0, 3.9 Setting)
55 ML bloom 45 seconds 
Swirl immediately after pour
Then 80 ML
Then At 1.30 again 80 ML
Then again 80 ML to finish it off with gentle swirl in the end.

Water at 94° Celsius (TDS not more than 140 PPM).

name: Pink Lemonade (Ultra-Light)
description:
#5 SERIES - HIGH SCORING LOTS | Harvest 2026 | Pink Lemonade

Lemonade like with Sweet & lively acidity.

Suitable for all brew methods. Ideal as Filter. 

Fruity Citrus Indian Arabica Coffee.

Serving as Pour-over at Bandra, Mumbai & Pune, Koregoan Park
Origin Tsiesema Village, Kohima, Nagaland
Process Sun-Dried Anaerobic Naturals with Raised Bed Drying.
Varietal & Altitude Chandragiri grown at 1350 MSL
Dry Aroma Blueberries, Pineapples & Chocolate
Pre-crust Aroma Dried Figs & Apples
Post-crust Aroma Jackfruit, Nuts & Dates.
Sensory Evaluation Vibrant citrus characters, layered with orange, green grape & red apple atop a sweet base of dried fig.
Roast Profile Ultra-Light roast with elevated heat & restrained airflow, developed to 16%
Characteristics Sweet, lively acidity with Med-heavy body & Bright aromatic lift
Minimum resting period Filter 5 Days | Espresso 9 Days
A song that pairs well

 

Roaster thoughts :

We approached the roast with elevated initial energy and restrained airflow, allowing the coffee to move cleanly through drying while avoiding excessive convection that can flatten aromatics. The profile was kept deliberately short, finishing at an ultra-light endpoint with 15-16% development, just enough to stabilise the structure without muting the fruit.Anaerobic coffees can easily tip into heavy, ferment-driven profiles. Here, we aimed for the opposite, keeping the cup transparent and articulate, where fermentation supports rather than dominates. In the cup, this results in a bright citrus-forward expression, with orange and green grape acidity, layered with red apple sweetness, and a softer fig-like finish that carries through the aftertaste. The body remains medium-heavy but clean, with a lifted aromatic profile.

Brewing Note: Due to its delicate roast level, we recommend brewing this coffee with higher water temperatures (97-98°C) and a controlled pour to ensure full extraction. Attention to grind size, agitation, and brew time is critical to achieve optimal clarity and balance in the cup.

This coffee is a testament to our commitment to innovation and continuous refinement in roasting. 

Brew Better: Water & Resting Guidelines

Dose: 18g
Water: 270g (1:15 ratio)
Temperature: 97–98°C
Grind: Medium (slightly finer than your standard V60)
Brew Time: 2:30 – 2:50

For more citrus brightness
→ go coarser + faster drawdown

For more sweetness & body
→ go finer + extend brew to ~3:00

Water is just as important as the beans. For the cleanest, most balanced cup, we recommend using **mineral water with a Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) level not above 140 ppm**. This will allow the true flavor of your coffee to shine.

Rested Coffee = Better Coffee

Freshly roasted coffee continues to evolve. Harsh or roasty notes fade, giving way to sweetness, clarity, and complexity.

Our resting guide:

Minimum rest (Filter): 5 days after roast date
Minimum rest (Espresso): Up to 9 weeks after roast date

Patience pays off. Let your coffee settle, and enjoy a cup that truly reflects its origin.

name: Cane and Lime (Light-Med Roast)
description:
#2 SERIES - ROASTERS ART | Harvest 2026 | Cane & Lime

Dense & Sugar-driven flavours in your final cup.

Suitable for all brew methods. Sweet & Bright Indian Arabica Coffee.

Origin Yelnoorkhan Estate, Pandaravalli Village, Mallenahalli
Process High altitude washed arabica dried on raised beds.
Varietal & Altitude Chandragiri grown at 5300 Feet
Dry Aroma Dates & Chickoo
Pre Crust Aroma Cardamon, Green Grapes & Dates
Post Crust Aroma Chickoo, Milk Chocolate & Raisins
Based on Sensory Evaluation

Sweet lime & gooseberry brightness, layered over dense sugar-driven base of jaggery & sugarcane
Roast Profile Light-Medium Roast with high air flow & 14-15 % development.
Characteristics

Juicy mouthfeel with a medium body &
bright, clean acidity.
Minimum resting period Filter 7 Days | Espresso 14 Days
A song that pairs well

 

About the region / estate :

At a maximum elevation of 5300 feet above MSL, the coffees from the Yelnoorkhan Estate are in a class of their own. These high elevation coffees are much sought-after and have the rare distinction of having been sold under the Yelnoor Khan Mist brand name in North America in the early 2000s.

Established in the early 1900s, this estate was taken over by Kelachandra Coffee in 2021. Located in the direct vicinity of the Mullayanagiri peak, it tells the story of the history and origins of coffee culture in India. Due to the terrain’s harsh demands, handpicked coffee continues to remain a uniquely Indian tradition, even as the rest of the world moves on to mechanization. The ethos of respect for the land and the crop directly translates into one of Kelachandra Coffee’s finest single-origin produce. 

Roasters thought :

High elevation coffees tend to carry tighter cell structure and higher organic acid content. To manage this, we used high airflow throughout the roast, allowing for cleaner heat transfer and avoiding any roast-induced heaviness that could mask the cup’s definition.

The profile was taken to a light–medium endpoint with ~14% development, giving just enough time to round off sharper acids while maintaining the coffee’s natural brightness and juiciness.

Rather than extending development, we prioritised a clean and efficient Maillard phase, ensuring that sweetness builds without muting the acidity.

In the cup, this translates to a structured citrus profile, where sweet lime and gooseberry define the front, supported by a dense, sugarcane and jaggery-driven sweetness.

Brew Approach:

18.5 GMS Med-Fine (Fellow Ode Gen 2.0, 3.9 Setting)
55 ML bloom 45 seconds 
Swirl immediately after pour
Then 80 ML
Then At 1.30 again 80 ML
Then again 95 ML to finish it off with gentle swirl in the end.

Water at 94° Celsius (TDS not more than 140 PPM).

For more brightness (lime forward)
→ go slightly coarser + reduce final pour agitation

For more sweetness (jaggery heavy)
→ grind finer + extend brew closer to 2:50

name: MOGRA
description:
#5 SERIES - HIGH SCORING LOTS | MOGRA

Jasmine in your final cup.

Suitable for all brew methods. Ideal as Filter. Indian Arabica Coffee.

Serving as

Pour-over at Bandra, Mumbai
Origin Ratnagiri Estate, Chikmagalur
Process Anaerobic Fermented Naturals with culture microbes & mechanical dried at the farm.
Varietal & Altitude
SL9 grown at 4450 Feet
Dry Aroma Jasmine Florals, Chocolate & Grapefuit
Wet Aroma Jasmine, Vanilla & Forest Honey.
BRIX 24.2
Sensory Evaluation
Intensely sweet cup with notes of Vanilla & Sweet Lime underpinning complex floral notes of Jasmine.
Roast Profile
Light Roast dropped with an early 1st crack & 16% DTR.
Characteristics
Heavy floral aromatics followed by a well balanced cup & deep sweetness.
Minimum resting period Filter 10 Days | Espresso 19 Days
A song that pairs well

 

Roaster thoughts :
Fermented naturals from ratnagiri estate profiled as an ultra light to bring out the floral notes from this LOT. This coffee is one the most unique single origin coffees's we have come across. A lot that everyone must try to understand terror and complexity Indian specialty coffee can deliver. It was a challenge at first to understand the nature, origin and process of this LOT, but as we sample roasted and cupped first few batches we knew where we were headed. Clean floral aromatics, jasmine in your final cup & bright acidity makes this a very enjoyable cup of coffee. 

Brewing Note: Due to its delicate roast level, we recommend brewing this coffee with higher water temperatures (97°C) and a controlled pour to ensure full extraction. Attention to grind size, agitation, and brew time is critical to achieve optimal clarity and balance in the cup.

This coffee is a testament to our commitment to innovation and continuous refinement in roasting. 

The estate and efforts:
We all are familiar with the producer Mr. Ashok Patre and his family run estate Ratnagiri Estate. Our founder visited the farm back in the month of march 2021 when coffee processing was at its peak.
A day's visit to the estate to understand the farm, the processing techniques and the history behind the legacy was great. Our meeting began with knowing each other and talking and about the passion that runs Grey Soul Coffee as a brand.
Then it led to discussions about the specialty community and culture in our country right now. Moving on, we spoke about cup score, Q grading and how it varies from person to person and hence become highly subjective.
Then we spoke about international markets and a comparison between Indian and south American coffee. Then quickly moved on a long elaborate your of the farm where some coffee was milled and ready, some drying on raised beds, some drying out in the fields and hand garbling in works as final sorting was in process.
In the end, specialty coffee can be simply defined as the coffee that is of the best quality without comprises. This is exactly what this estate stands for and believes in.

Brew Better: Water & Resting Guidelines

Water is just as important as the beans. For the cleanest, most balanced cup, we recommend using **mineral water with a Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) level not above 140 ppm**. This will allow the true flavor of your coffee to shine.

Rested Coffee = Better Coffee

Freshly roasted coffee continues to evolve. Harsh or roasty notes fade, giving way to sweetness, clarity, and complexity.

Our resting guide:

Minimum rest (Filter): 10 days after roast date
Minimum rest (Espresso): Up to 3 weeks after roast date

Patience pays off. Let your coffee settle, and enjoy a cup that truly reflects its origin.

name: Summer in Kodaikanal (Light Roast)
description:
#1 SERIES - FRUIT FORWARD LOTS | Harvest 2026 | SUMMER IN KODAIKANAL

Mandarin brightness & rounded body that carries a lingering tropical fruit finish.

Suitable for all brew methods. Fruity Indian Arabica Coffee.

Origin Princess of Hill Stations (Kodaikanal), Perumalmalai Hills, St. Joseph Estate
Process Sun Dried Naturals using Controlled Dehydrator Drying
Varietal & Altitude Catimor, Chandragiri & Sln9 grown at 4000+ Feet
Dry Aroma Ripe Red berries
Pre Crust Aroma Plums & Pineapples
Post Crust Aroma Red Berries & Oranges
Based on Sensory Evaluation

Ripe Strawberries with mandarin brightness, layered over gentle tropical fruit & soft cacao finish.
Roast Profile Light Roast with high air flow & 14% development
Characteristics

Sweet, vibrant cup with bright acidity,
a medium-heavy body & lingering sweetness.
Minimum resting period Filter 6 Days | Espresso 14 Days
A song that pairs well

 

About the region / estate :

This lot was sourced from St. Joseph Estate, situated in the hills of Perumalmalai in Kodaikanal, a region often referred to as the Princess of Hill Stations. The estate sits at approximately 4000 feet above sea level, where cooler mountain temperatures allow for slower cherry maturation and a more concentrated sugar development in the fruit.

The coffee is composed of Catimore, Chandragiri, and SLN9 cultivars, varieties well suited to the high elevation conditions of the region. Cherries were harvested at peak ripeness and processed as sun-dried naturals, using controlled dehydrator technology to carefully regulate moisture loss during the drying phase. This method allows for a stable fermentation environment while preserving the integrity of the fruit sugars and aromatic compounds.

Roasters thought :

During roasting, we aimed to highlight the coffee’s natural fruit density and creamy structure. The profile follows a light roast approach with elevated airflow and a development ratio of approximately 14%, allowing for clarity of flavour while maintaining the underlying sweetness and tactile body.

In the cup, the coffee expresses a profile reminiscent of strawberries and cream, supported by a soft mandarin-like acidity and layered tropical fruit undertones. The acidity is sweet and rounded rather than sharp, and the mouthfeel develops into a medium to medium-heavy body with a smooth, almost velvety texture.

Roast Profile:

Sample Roast Machine : Bullet IBTS R1
Roast Machine : Probat VFD

Development % : 14
First Crack Temperature : Below 194° Celsius 

Brew Approach:

19 GMS Med-Fine (Fellow Ode Gen 2.0, 3.9 Setting)
55 ML bloom 45 seconds 
Swirl immediately after pour
Then 80 ML
Then At 1.30 again 80 ML
Then again 95 ML to finish it off with gentle swirl in the end.

Water at 97° Celsius (TDS not more than 140 PPM).

name: Raspberry in Loop
description:
#2 SERIES - ROASTERS ART | 2.3 RASPBERRY IN LOOP 

Heavy Bodied with Raspberry tartiness in your final cup.

Suitable for all brew methods. Fruity Indian Arabica Coffee.

Origin Chikmagalur, Karnataka
Process Anaerobic fermentation done in 3 stages for 72 hours , 48 hours and 24 hours consecutively. Eventually sun-dried on raised beds for a extended period.
BRIX 22 
Varietal & Altitude Sl795 & Chandragiri grown at 4180 ft
Dry Aroma Pineapple, Mandarin & Cacao
Wet Aroma Prune & Chocolate
Sensory Evaluation

Natural lot with rich & ripe character of Raspberry backed up by round milk chocolate contrasted with a crisp & sweet mandarin acidity.
Roast Profile Med Roast with high DTR, low fan speed & variable drum RPM.
Characteristics Heavy bodied with deep rich tart sweetness.
Minimum resting period Filter 7 Days | Espresso 14 Days
A song that pairs well

 

Roaster thoughts :
After Mango in Loop & strawberry comes in a single origin arabica called Raspberry in Loop. We’ve taken this to a medium roast with a high development time ratio, keeping fan speed low and drum RPM variable. This gives us heavier caramelisation and excellent solubility, while still preserving a bright, clean thread of acidity. In the cup, expect a rich, ripe raspberry core supported by pineapple and mandarin up top. It’s heavy-bodied, dense and sweet, ideal for both syrupy, fruit-forward espresso and big, expressive filter brews. We recommend resting 7 days for filter and around 14 days for espresso to let the aromatics settle and the sweetness really lock in.

Brew Approach :

18 Gram -> 40 ML (1:2.15)
Temperature 91-93 C
Extraction time 25 sec
Steady pressure of 9

Pressure profiling,
Start: 2 bars → 6 bars at 10 sec → hold at 9 bars from 10–30 sec

Brew Better: Water & Resting Guidelines

Water is just as important as the beans. For the cleanest, most balanced cup, we recommend using **mineral water with a Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) level not above 140 ppm**. This will allow the true flavor of your coffee to shine.

Rested Coffee = Better Coffee

Freshly roasted coffee continues to evolve. Harsh or roasty notes fade, giving way to sweetness, clarity, and complexity.

Our resting guide:

Minimum rest (Filter): 7 days after roast date
Minimum rest (Espresso): Up to 2-3 weeks after roast date

Patience pays off. Let your coffee settle, and enjoy a cup that truly reflects its origin.

description:
#2 ROASTERS ART | ROASTERS ESPRESSO 3.0

Well rounded Heavy Body with a base of sweet & creamy milk chocolate.

Suitable for all brew methods. Medium Roast Espresso Indian Arabica Coffee.

Serving as House blend at Grey Soul Coffee Roasters, Koregoan Park, Pune.
Origin Chikmagalur, Karnataka

A song that pairs well

 

Roaster's thought :
Roasters art a series created by Grey Soul Coffee Roasters to showcase our strength which is roasting Indian specialty arabica and also the mastery of profiling and blending different single origin coffee. The new roasters espresso 3.0 is ideal to have as an espresso, americano, cortado and cappuccino's. A different approach to roasting is what we adapted to this lot and is what we call extended maillard technique. In this particular way, we start off the roast at a lower temperature and gradually increase post the dry end phase which allows the coffee to roast longer during the browning phase thus producing the sweet acidity, denser crema and long lasting finish.

Freshly roasted coffee continues to evolve. Harsh or roasty notes fade, giving way to sweetness, clarity, and complexity.

Minimum rest (Espresso): Up to 3 weeks after roast date

name: Kerehaklu Estate - Blossom Culture
description:
With the estate shrouded in fog on a January morning, Pranoy noticed unseasonal blossoms in one of the blocks. There, he had the idea of collecting jarfuls of these blossoms for a starter culture. The goal was to see what happens when Kerehaklu's own microbiome shapes processing. 
 
Aiding a 71-hour anoxic fermentation, the blossom culture interacted with naturally processed cherries to build fruity layers and a distinctive jamminess. To preserve this development, the coffee was dried on raised beds for three weeks. 
 
Roasted to a light profile, the result is a unique expression of provenance. The cup opens with the aroma of ripe berries, followed by notes of strawberry, orange blossom, pomegranate, and sun melon. A delicate floral finish rounds off each sip.

Recommended Resting Period: 12 days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Howdia Estate
description:
One of our roasters' favourites, Howdia Estate returns for Harvest '26. It reminds us of a floral black tea, and is among the most delicate light roasts on our roster. Processed using the washed method, it brews cups with low bitterness, bright acidity, and a well-rounded mouthfeel. From the first whiff, it's florality comes through, giving way to a bright, tea-like sip with notes of coffee blossoms and orange marmalade, and a black tea-like finish. For a clean, nuanced cup, we recommend brewing this coffee black as a pour over or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 days

name: Elkhill Estates
description:
Our debut coffee from Elkhill, a group of estates spanning 1500 acres, this anaerobic washed lot comes from their first year of specialty cultivation. It brews balanced cups with layers of fruit and spice, and a subtle hint of nuts.

Ripe cherries, harvested at elevations between 457 to 1067 MASL, were fermented for 36 hours. Next, they were washed then slow-dried on raised beds for nearly 18 days to preserve their character.   

Roasted to a medium profile, the result is a cup that opens with the aroma of brown sugar and roasted almonds. Each sip is reminiscent of orange, brown spice, and roasted hazelnut, and ends in a lingering, orange zest-like finish.

Our roasters recommend brewing this coffee as an espresso, a cold brew, or using a Moka Pot. It tastes great black and also works well with milk.

Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

name: Araku - Viishalakshi FPC
description:
Every harvest brings the excitement of new partnerships and new coffees. This season, we’re proud to introduce our debut lot from Viishalakshi Farmer Producer Company (FPC) in Araku Valley. Named after the valley’s wide-eyed goddess, the FPC brings together 33 
tribal villages around Kusumaguda. This lot comes from seven of those villages, where coffee cultivation is led by women and processed at a communal facility. 

Rooted in natural farming practices for generations, the farmers use composted fruit and vegetable waste to nourish the soil and neem oil treatments to safeguard against pests. Formed last year, Vishalakshi has helped guide these villages from commercial coffee cultivation towards specialty practices. There is now a growing focus on pruning plants, selective picking, proper storage of beans, and careful processing.  

Roasted to a medium profile, this honey sun-dried lot brews clean, balanced cups. It opens with brown sugar and melon, giving way to roasted almonds, prunes, and a whisper of brown spice. The body is round and syrupy; the finish is long and zesty.  

We recommend brewing it as an espresso, or using a French Press or Channi. It tastes great black as well as with milk.

Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

Note: This coffee pack has limited availability and therefore cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Raxidi Lobo Estate - Anaerobic Natural
description:
We've been excited to collaborate with Raxidi Lobo Estate since their debut with us last year. So, when we first tasted a sample of this anaerobic natural lot, we knew it had to be a part of Harvest '26.  

To bring it to life, the producers started fermenting some of the season's best cherries. Introducing a specially curated yeast strain to the mix, they let the process go on for 48 hours. Finally, slow drying on raised beds for 21 days locked flavour.  

Roasted to a medium profile, the result is a cup that carries the sweet nostalgia of drinking mosambi juice in summer. It opens with berries and cherry on the nose, then settles into tart-sweet, bright notes of mosambi, green apple, and plum. The mouthfeel is velvety with a medium body, and the finish is long and tea-like.  

Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as a pour over, or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

Note: This coffee pack has limited availability and therefore cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Kerehaklu Estate
description:
Harvest '26 debuts with a bright, citrusy light roast. A Kerehaklu special, it shows Pranoy and Ajoy's sure hand with washed processing. 

Ripe red Selection 9 cherries collected by seasoned pickers marked the lot's foundation. The producers then used a starter made from the farm's local microbes to aid fermentation. Monitoring temperature and pH regularly, they finished within 37 hours. Next, the coffee was mechanically washed and dried in the shade for three days. Finally, 12 days of polyhouse drying on raised beds locked its flavour. This controlled, aerobic washed process built complexity while harnessing the bean's inherent character.  

Roasted to a light profile, the coffee delivers clean cups that open with the aroma of orange blossoms and brown sugar. Notes of orange, black tea, and green grapes follow, wrapped in a juicy mouthfeel. Expect low bitterness, medium-high acidity, and a lingering finish of orange marmalade.  

Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as a pour over, or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 12 Days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Half - Caff
description:
Our first-ever single-origin, specialty Half-Caff comes from Yelnoorkhan Estate. We selected their S795, washed processed coffee to create a complex and distinctive cup.  

To reduce caffeine by 55%, we used CO₂ decaffeination, a chemical-free, minimal-waste generating method that is conscious in its water and energy usage. We chose it because the other decaffeination methods available to us in India came with a catch. In removing all the caffeine, they also took away the depth that makes a cup memorable. Adding artificial flavours was not something we wanted to do, never mind the fact that many of these methods also used far too much water.  

The result is a cup with a gentler kick that holds its own in terms of flavour. You’ll first notice chocolate biscuits on the nose as well as your palate. A silky mouthfeel then reveals notes of roasted hazelnuts and malt, followed by a long, nutty finish. 

For the best experience, brew this coffee using an espresso machine. It tastes great black and is equally suited to milk-based beverages.

Recommended Resting Period: 5 Days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Sandalwood Estate
description:
A beloved part of our perennial selection, Sandalwood Estate brews cups with tasting notes of rich dark chocolate, sweet prune and zesty orange marmalade. This washed coffee, with coffee beans of the Sarchimor variety, was grown at a lush coffee estate in Coorg. If you’ve tried our coffees from Attikan and Baarbara Estates, you’ll love the chocolatey flavour profile of this medium-dark roast.  

This heavy bodied coffee has a smooth, syrupy mouthfeel which can best be enjoyed when brewed as an espresso or using a Moka Pot or French Press. The long, sweet aftertaste of butter biscuits and dried fruit comes through beautifully when you allow the brew to cool down a little. 

Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

name: Monsoon Malabar AA- Hoysala Estate
description:
We’re excited to bring back Monsoon Malabar from Hoysala Estate. The unique flavour profile of this coffee develops when winds and humidity from seasonal monsoon rain change the characteristics of the coffee beans. While this process has its accidental roots in colonial India when a shipment to Europe was attacked by the full force of monsoon winds, similar conditions have been recreated in a controlled environment for consistency in every lot produced. 

When roasted medium-dark, the result is a medium-bodied cup that invites with sweet aromas of butter biscuits, treating you to notes of cocoa nibs and dried fruit, concluding with the aftertaste of dark chocolate. Best enjoyed when brewed as an espresso, in the Moka Pot or the French press, the nutty flavour profile of this coffee makes for a delicious cup, either with milk or black. 

Recommended Resting Period: 15 Days

name: Dhak Blend
description:
Our Dhak Blend is an ode to one of our favourite Indian trees with its colorful flame-like flowers that signal the onset of Spring. The coffees used in this blend are naturally processed which means that the coffee beans are dried with the cherry, resulting in complex, fruity and sweet flavours.

Roasted dark to bring out flavours of dark chocolate and fruit jam, this blend's heavy cocoa body leaves a smooth lingering aftertaste.

Our roasting team recommends the Dhak Blend for espresso-based drinks as well as manual brews such as the Moka Pot and the French Press.

Recommended Resting Period: 9 Days

name: Attikan Estate
description:
Attikan Estate’s arabica coffee beans come from the Biligiriranga Hills in Karnataka and make for one of our most popular coffees. Sweet with nutty overtones and balanced acidity, this is the darkest of our standard medium roasts and recommended for espresso lovers. It is a versatile coffee that also works for manual brewing methods such as Moka Pot, South Indian Filter and AeroPress. 

Located to the south of Mysore, the Biligiriranga Hills, or ‘white hills’ are named after the mist that hangs over the region. At 1650 meters, it is amongst the highest coffee growing regions in India and grows Selection 9, Selection 795, Cauvery and Kent varieties of Arabica, along with Silver Oaks, citrus, and fig trees.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 Days

name: Mooleh Manay Estate – CM Natural
description:
Returning to our Producer Series after 2023, Komal Sable and Akshay Dashrath share their first experiment with carbonic maceration. Building on the clarity and consistency they achieved with anaerobic fermentation last season, the fifth-generation producers modified their drums to create a CO₂-rich, oxygen-free environment that allows for slower, more controlled fermentation within whole cherries. 

The process began by removing floaters to select only ripe, dense cherries, followed by a brief pre-drying phase to reduce surface moisture. The cherries were then sealed in drums, and a custom culture was introduced to extend the fermentation. Over 60 hours, this combination of carbonic maceration and yeast inoculation ensured thorough mucilage breakdown and the development of deep complexity. 

Post-fermentation, the cherries were dried on raised beds inside a polyhouse. Continuous raking over 7 to 10 days ensured even drying until a final moisture level of 11–12% was reached. 

Roasted light by Rishab from our team, this coffee offers a well-structured cup with notes of fermented red fruit and a bright, juicy sweetness. It opens with the aroma of mixed berries and carries a syrupy mouthfeel, with layered flavours of dried fig, plum, black grape, and mulberry. A chocolatey aftertaste marks the finish, adding further depth. 

We recommend brewing this expressive coffee black, as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 16 Days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.

name: 13th Birthday Blend
description:
This celebratory blend brings together natural lots from Stanmore, Orchardale, and Riverdale Estates in Yercaud, along with a washed lot from Unakki Estate in Chikmagalur, which forms the base. Its flavour profile takes us back to the Black Forest cakes many of us celebrated birthdays with during our teen years. 

Opening with the aroma of honey and strawberries, the cup has a medium-high body and a round mouthfeel. You'll notice notes of strawberry, chocolate, cherry, and pear, followed by a lingering finish of chocolate-covered strawberries. 

This blend brews well across a range of methods, including espresso, AeroPress, French Press, Moka Pot, and Pour Over. Equally enjoyable black or with milk, it lends itself to a wide range of recipes.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 Day

name: SKIA Coffee (Pack of 2)
description:
This two-pack (100 gms each) brings together distinct coffees from Nelaji Village in Coorg. Grown by smallholder farmers and processed by Ashish Rao, a first-generation producer, these lots mark our first collaboration with Skia Coffee. 

Ripe, high-density cherries were pulped with the mucilage left intact, then placed in sealed tanks for a 72-hour anaerobic fermentation. A yeast strain purpose-built for controlled fermentation was introduced during this stage to develop complexity. 

From there, the two lots took separate paths. 

Honey Sun Dried  

The first lot was dried slowly on raised beds under controlled shade. Roasted to a medium profile, it makes for a balanced cup with notes of sweet lime, prunes, and almond. 

Recommended Resting Period: 16 Days

Thermal Shock  

This second lot was immersed in hot water, then rapidly cooled in ice. It was then mechanically washed and dried slowly under shade. Also roasted to a medium profile, it brews cups with notes of tangerine, brown sugar, and berries.  

Both coffees brew beautifully as an espresso or with an AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press. They taste great black and pair well with milk. Together, they offer a chance to explore how thoughtful shifts in processing shape flavour in the final cup.  

Recommended Resting Period: 12 Days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.

name: Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective
description:
It's always exciting for us to partner with a new farm. With Meghalaya's Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective, that excitement runs even deeper. A completely new coffee growing region for us, it speaks of the possibilities that the North East Indian soil holds for specialty production. The collective’s origin goes back a decade, when Daman, a first-generation coffee producer, visited Nongryniang—a remote village in Khasi Hills and home to the nanny who cared for him in his early years. 

"There, nestled among the misty hills, I came across two old coffee plants growing in someone’s backyard. I later learned that back in the 1980s, the government had briefly launched a coffee planting program in the area. Like many such initiatives, it had long been abandoned and forgotten. But those plants stayed with me. And so did the people.", he recounts. Since then, Daman started a decade-long pursuit of craft and community. From shading systems to post-harvest processing, he spent years learning all it takes to grow high-quality coffee. Over time, the collective has grown in both, resolve and numbers, with 75 farmers now contributing to a harvest. They pick only the ripest cherries by hand, which are sun-dried for 15–22 days depending on weather conditions.  

The first coffee that we’ve sourced from the collective is a natural lot we’ve chosen to roast to a medium profile. It brews cups that open with the aroma of raisins, unfolding into a creamy mouthfeel. Notes of blueberry, black tea, and khasi mandarin carry through in each sip, with a long, marmalade-like finish. A balanced coffee, it lends well to various brewing methods, including espresso, Moka Pot, French Press, and AeroPress. It is enjoyable on its own as well as in milk-based beverages.

Recommended Resting Period: 13 Days

name: Kolli Berri Estate
description:
Our first coffee from Harvest ‘24 is a medium-dark roast with chocolatey and nutty flavours. This single-origin ground coffee hails from the beautiful Kolli Berri Estate, set in Chikmagalur, Karnataka. 

While brewing this one, you’ll notice the unique characteristics of the coffee beans, starting with the aroma of dried fruits, followed by a syrupy mouthfeel in every sip. With medium acidity and medium- high bitterness, it offers a full-bodied profile which is enhanced when brewed as an espresso or using an AeroPress, Moka Pot or a French Press.

name: Amruthavarshini Estate
description:
Meet our second release by Amruthavarshini Estate, a women-led estate run by a mother-daughter duo. Processed using the anaerobic natural method, this medium roast brews fruity and nutty cups with a pleasant sweetness.  

A honey-like aroma leads into bright notes of cherries and pineapples. The nuttiness of roasted almonds adds depth, while the mouthfeel remains syrupy. In the finish, you’ll taste the lingering aftertaste of raisins and nuts.  

Our roasters recommend brewing it as an espresso, a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. It tastes great whether you enjoy it black or with milk.

Recommended Resting Period: 12 Days

name: The Teenage Trail - Box of 13 Coffees
description:
This limited-release marks our first teen year, bringing together thirteen of our most-loved brews from across regions, roast levels, and flavour profiles. And if you've been meaning to give your coffee routine a stir, this is a great place to start. You'll revisit cups that you have returned to over the years while finding new favourites along the way.

The selection includes 30g tasting jars of:

Garigekhan Estate

A bright, layered cup showcasing Castillo, a resilient Arabica variety created specifically to combat leaf rust.

Roast Level: Light | Processing: Washed| Tasting Notes: Grapefruit, Pomegranate, Cherry

Riverdale Estate – Aroma

A layered, fruit-forward cup, bright with the aroma of berries and pineapple.

Roast Level: Light | Processing: Natural | Tasting Notes: Floral, Candy, Berries

Seethargundu Estate

A delicate and complex coffee from a Demeter-certified estate that treats their land as a living ecosystem, nurturing soil health, biodiversity, and long-term balance.

Roast Level: Light | Processing: Washed | Tasting Notes: Sweet Lime, Black Tea, Stone Fruit

Baarbara Estate – Intenso Yeast

An experimental lot processed with intenso yeast, a yeast usually used by beer brewers.

Roast Level: Light | Processing: Natural | Tasting Notes: Strawberry, Red Currant, Rose

13th Birthday Blend

A limited-edition reminiscent of the Black Forest cakes many of us celebrated teen birthdays with.

Roast Level: Medium | Processing: Washed + Natural | Tasting Notes: Cherry, Chocolate, Strawberry, Pear

Silver Oak Blend

Our signature blend that brings a little of our cafe experience to you.

Roast Level: Medium | Processing: Washed + Natural | Tasting Notes: Hazelnut, Honey, Grapes

Amruthavarshini Estate

A fruity and nutty coffee, sourced from a women-led estate.

Roast Level: Medium | Processing: Natural | Tasting Notes: Cherries, Pineapples, Roasted Almonds

MSP Orchardale Estate

A fruity and punchy coffee from the misty high peaks of Yercaud.

Roast Level: Medium | Processing: Natural | Tasting Notes: Caramel, Cherry, Chocolate

Attikan Estate

A favourite among homebrewers with nutty overtones and balanced acidity.

Roast Level: Medium-Dark | Processing: Washed | Tasting Notes: Dark Chocolate, Figs, Roaster Almonds

St. Joseph’s Estate

Our first release from a partner farm run by Jesuit priests in the Palani Hills, Tamil Nadu.

Roast Level: Medium-Dark | Processing: Washed | Tasting Notes: Grapefruit, Clove, Toffee

Monsoon Malabar

A timeless delight, as rich in flavour as history.

Roast Level: Medium-Dark | Processing: Monsooned | Tasting Notes: Cocoa Nibs, Nutty, Raisins

Vienna Roast

Our most-loved dark roast, perfect for those who enjoy a bold cup.

Roast Level: Dark | Processing: Washed | Tasting Notes: Cocoa, Oaky, Bittersweet

Dhak Blend

An ode to one of our favourite flowers with colourful flame-like flowers that signal the onset of Spring.

Roast Level: Dark | Processing: Natural | Tasting Notes: Dark Chocolate, Cocoa, Fruit Jam

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Winter Blend
description:
Meet the blend our roasters look forward to crafting each winter. Pairing well with milk, it is also a solid base for all those winter recipes you've been saving.

We've created it using a careful mix of natural and washed lots from St. Joseph Estate and Attikan Estate. Opening with the aroma of brown spices, this coffee has a medium body and a syrupy, round mouthfeel. You’ll be able to taste cinnamon, cacao, roasted almonds, and raisins, and tying everything together nicely is a chocolatey aftertaste.

We recommend brewing it as an espresso, or with a Moka Pot or French Press.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 Days

name: Krishnagiri Estate
description:
A single origin dark roast, this coffee comes from a Rainforest Alliance Certified farm. The producers used a custom-designed pulper to process this washed lot, minimising water usage.  

In the cup, you'll first notice the aroma of brown spices. The brew, characterised by mellow acidity, a heavy body, and a velvety mouthfeel, reminds of oak, toasted walnuts, and malt. A bittersweet finish lingers between sips.  

We recommend brewing this coffee as an espresso, using a Moka Pot, French Press, or an AeroPress. It is rich enough to enjoy black, and also pairs well with milk.

Recommended Resting Period: 7 Days

name: Speciality Single Origin Bababudangiri Region
description:
Embark on a remarkable journey through the rich heritage of coffee cultivation in the hallowed grounds of Baba Budan Giri hills. This renowned destination, named after the legendary merchant Baba Budan, who deftly transported precious coffee seeds from Yemen, stands as the embodiment of India's esteemed coffee culture.

Immerse yourself in our exceptional roast, where you will discover a delightful interplay of flavors. Experience the gentle sweetness of juicy passionfruit balanced by the lively brightness of pineapple. As the temperature gradually descends, a captivating essence of richer molasses emerges, offering a truly indulgent sensation.

This coffee is meticulously crafted through a natural processing method, wherein the coffee beans are dried alongside the cherry, resulting in a remarkable symphony of complex, fruity, and sweet flavors. Only the finest, fully ripened cherries are meticulously handpicked, expertly sorted, and sun-dried on African raised beds, ensuring a pristine and flawless quality.

name: Fruits Bomb
description:
Fruits Bomb 2026 is now available—our new-harvest release from Ratnagiri Estate, shipped straight from Karnataka through our direct-trade, sustainable relationship. Sourced from the Jeri Patte block at 1,350 MASL and yielded from the Catuai varietal, this release continues Savorworks’ flagship story that coffee enthusiasts have followed since 2020. True to its name, it’s a bomb of fruits.

Only fully ripe cherries were picked, sorted, and cleaned. At 25.9 Brix, floaters were removed before sequential inoculation with lab-grown cultures and a 54-hour anaerobic fermentation in bio-reactors. Post-fermentation, the coffee went directly to raised beds and dried slowly with constant stirring for 26 days building layered fruit expression. We roast it medium-light in Delhi to preserve processing character, elevate sweetness, and keep the profile balanced with an extra-long finish.

In the cup, expect grilled pineapple brightness with a touch of caramelized sweetness, umeshu-like depth from fermentation, a clear blueberry lift, and a gentle floral aroma. The body is juicy, the sweetness balanced yet complex, and the aftertaste long and wine-like, roasted for those seeking a standout experience. We highly recommend you taste it for yourself.

"The journey of Fruits Bomb began during the pandemic of 2020, when the first batch was personally delivered door-to-door by our founder, marking the start of a fruity profile coffee story. Now, it’s a favorite among friends of Savorworks, with recurring orders that celebrate our commitment to quality."

FACTS:

Estate: Ratnagiri Estate

Altitude: 1350 MASL

Varietal: CATUAI

Process: Lab Grown Cultures -  Naturals

Roast Level-  Medium Light

Roast Rite Color (Whole Bean): 73

Roast Rite Color (Ground): 87

 

FEELS:

Tasting Notes: Grilled Pineapple, Umeshu, Blueberry, Cherry Blossom

Body: Juicy

Aftertaste: Very Long

name: Honey I'm Nuts
description:
Coffee that's bound to drive you nuts and keep you buzzing for more! These coffees have been carefully grown and nurtured at Ratnagiri Estate in Chikmagalur, Karnataka, which has a long and faithful global following.

The coffee from the Giri Patte block, sequentially fermented and washed. Whole cherries ferment anaerobically for 24 hours, then are depulped and fermented aerobically for 24 hours with Mosto (fresh mucilage must). The coffee is then washed and slow-dried for 14 days for high-quality clarity and refined sweetness. This washed process brings out a very balanced cup with a lot of subtle flavours, bright acidity, and silky body, with flavours like yellow lemon, apricot, fig, and jaggery. 

Its uniqueness is bound to make it a daily "caffeine quencher" to keep you buzzing and drive you nuts with every sip.

Facts:

Origin: Ratnagiri Estate
Altitude: 1350 MASL
Varietal: SLN-9 & SLN-795
Process: Anaerobic Mosto Washed

Feels:

Tasting Notes: Yellow Lemon, Apricot, Fig, Jaggery
Acidity: Citric
Body: Juicy
Aftertaste: Medium

Roast Rite Color (Ground): 76
Roast Level: Medium

name: Riverdale Estate: Yercaud, Tamil Nadu | Double Ferment Natural| Light Roast
description:
Single Origin Arabica Micro lot from Riverdale Estate, Tamil Nadu, India

Light Roast (200g)

Process: Double Fermented Natural

Varietal: SLN9

Agtron Meter: 88

Best Suited: Filter Roast

Cupper's Notes: White Wine, Peach, Honey


Best Brewed With

Please note that the best brewed with list is not comprehensive and does not dictate that the coffees cannot be brewed with any other methods. These are the methods we think will extract the best possible cup. However, this coffee can be ground and enjoyed with any brew method that you desire.


Filter Roast

Manual brewing methods fall under the artisanal brewing style of coffee. Roasting coffee is also an art, we have developed this filter roast to maintain the quality while brewing over Pour over, Kalita, V60, Origami, April, and Chemex.

About The Process

At Riverdale Estate in the Shevaroy Hills, we meticulously handpick ripe coffee cherries with a Brix level of 25° or higher, ensuring optimal sweetness and flavour potential. Post-harvest, cherries undergo triple washing with natural spring water and density sorting to select only the most robust beans. We then infuse the cherries with Malabar plum (Syzygium cumini), a fruit rich in natural sugars and polyphenols, extending fermentation to 80 hours. This infusion enhances the coffee's acidity and fruity complexity. Following fermentation, cherries are sundried on raised beds for 30 days, promoting even drying and flavour development. The beans are then hulled, hand-sorted for quality, and vacuum-packed to maintain optimal moisture and freshness. This meticulous process yields a vibrant cup with delicate floral notes and a smooth, natural sweetness, reflecting our commitment to exceptional coffee craftsmanship.

About the Roast

Light Roast: At Subko, a light roast is one that is obtained by dropping the coffee lot at 186°-189°C. These roasts typically showcase a sensory profile that is delicate,floral and tea-like, and fruit-forward. In terms of the Agtron scale, Subko's definition of a light roast lies between the points 89 to 95, with 95 being the lightest version of a light roast.

Flavour Meter


Best Brewed With

FILTER ROAST


Please note that the best brewed with list is not comprehensive and does not dictate that the coffees cannot be brewed with any other methods. These are the the methods we think will extract the best possible cup. However, this coffee can be ground and enjoyed with any brew method that you desire.

Filter Roast: Manual brewing methods fall under the artisanal brewing style of coffee. Roasting a coffee is also an art, we have developed this filter roast to maintain the quality while brewing over Pour over, Kalita, V60, Origami, April, Chemex.
Culture naturals+ Anaerobic Naturals : -
RT- YC -1/1: This is a 72-hour CULTURE PROCESS natural processed coffee. It is from the CATUAI varietal grown on our farm at 4400 feet from the block called GODOWN Patte. The Brix of the coffee cherries was 25.4 when harvested and they were put in the Bio fermenters after floater removal. A particular strain of yeast and lactic acid bacteria was added to the coffee in the fermenters and allowed to ferment for 72 hours in a carbon dioxide rich environment. After removing the coffee, they were directly put on raised beds for slow drying. The coffee was then dried slowly with constant stirring over the next 29 days.


LAB PROCESS 07: This is a 60-hour anaerobic fermentation natural processed coffee. It is from the HEMAVTHI varietal grown on our farm at 4450 feet from the block called LINE Patte. The Brix of the coffee cherries was 23.9 when harvested and they were put in the Bio fermenters after floater removal and allowed to ferment for 60 hours in a Nitrogen rich environment with lab grown microbes isolated from the farm. After removing the coffee from the fermenters, it was directly put on raised beds for slow drying. The coffee was then dried slowly with constant stirring over the next 28 days.

About Project Pearl



In the Indian Specialty Coffee Industry, the name Ratnagiri Estate evinces a recognition of steadily elevating excellence, innovation, and a devotion to sustainability. The name Ratnagiri itself, translates to pearl mountain.


Over the years, Ratnagiri Estate's legacy in the Indian specialty coffee industry has steadily elevated as the flagbearers of specialty coffee growing, processing, and Indian specialty coffee representation overseas.


Today we’re honoured to be able to tell their story in the fullness of their legacy, with Project Pearl — a microlot program featuring 8 microlots from Ratnagiri Estate, exclusive only to Subko, that showcase the high-scoring, experimentally processed coffees that are a testament to their humble beginnings.

description:

Varietal: Excelsa

Agtron Meter: 63

Best Suited: Filter Roast

Cupper's Notes: Champagne, Green Grapes, Dry Dates.


Best Brewed With

FILTER ROAST

Manual brewing methods fall under the artisanal brewing style of coffee. Roasting a coffee is also an art, we have developed this filter roast to maintain the quality while brewing over Pour over, Kalita, V60, Origami, April, Chemex.

Please note that the best brewed with list is not comprehensive and does not dictate that the coffees cannot be brewed with any other methods. These are the the methods we think will extract the best possible cup. However, this coffee can be ground and enjoyed with any brew method that you desire.

About the Process

84 Hours Yeast Inoculated Natural : The coffee undergoes a meticulous process beginning with selective harvesting—only ripe cherries are hand-picked, sometimes using ladders—and cleaned via flotation to remove low-density beans and debris. The cherries then undergo 84 hours of carbonic maceration fermentation, inoculated with Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast to enhance flavor. After fermentation, the coffee is dried in a polyhouse, then moved to raised beds and raked regularly for even drying. Once moisture reaches 11–12%, the beans are carefully bagged for storage.

 

About the Roast

Medium Roast : At Subko, a Medium roast is one that is obtained by dropping the coffee lot at 201°-204°C. These roasts are generally of a sensory profile that is very smooth, caramel and complex tropical fruits. In terms of the Agtron scale, Subko's definition of medium lies between the points 60 to 74, with 74 being the lightest version of a medium roast, and 60 being the darkest version of the roast.

name: [Every Wednesday] The Pod Experience at The Cacao Mill: From The Farm to The Cacao Mill
description:
What is the beginning of the journey that makes Real Chocolate… which eventually melts?

The cracking open of the cacao pods. Sourced from the Indian Subcontinent, where transporting the pods from the farm to the city is a rarity.

This is what makes Craft Chocolate. This is where it all begins. And you can observe the process at The Cacao Mill. 

From cacao plantations in diverse regions in India, to the Experiential Table at The Cacao Mill - cracked open in front of you to scoop out cacao pulp that holds the flavor which makes a complex, snappy bar of chocolate. 


Venue: The Cacao Mill, Colaba

Dates:  Every Wednesday

Timings:  11 AM onwards

What to expect:

    The Pod Harvest Experience is a visual journey of the process of removal of pulp and then the beginning of the fermentation process. 

    Once the pods are cracked open and the cacao pulp is removed, the pulp is transported to The Cacao Mill Fermentation Tank. 

    As the Subko Cacao team loads the Fermentation Tank, golden elixir in the form of cacao juice starts to accumulate in the tank. 

    Taste the cacao juice, and watch The Pod Experience unfold at The Cacao Mill.

    Terms and Conditions
    • We love your company and we would be anticipating your arrival at least twenty minutes prior to the starting time.
    • Tickets once purchased are non-refundable.

name: Subko VLGE, Paderu, Andhra Pradesh | Gurram Hand Washed | Medium Roast
description:
Single Origin Specialty Arabica from SUBKO VLGE, Paderu, Andhra Pradesh

Medium Roast (250g)

Process: Gurram Hand Washed

Agtron Meter: 60

Altitude: 935 MASL

Varietal: Sln. 9

Cupper's Notes: Honey, Walnuts, Brown Sugar


Best Brewed With

ESPRESSO ROAST

Please note that the best brewed with list is not comprehensive and does not dictate that the coffees cannot be brewed with any other methods. These are the methods we think will extract the best possible cup. However, this coffee can be ground and enjoyed with any brew method that you desire.

About the Process

Gurram Hand Washed: The process, known as "Gurram Hand Washed," involves a small tribal community using their bare hands to pulp coffee fruits after fermentation. They then wash or demucilage the coffee with their hands.

Flavor Meter

Cupper's Notes

This coffee lot, roasted for an espresso brew or strong extraction, boasts a flavor profile reminiscent of sweet honey and walnuts, coupled with a heavy body. It features a prolonged, brown sugar-like finish and notes of caramel candy. The mellow, citric aftertaste is akin to that of a semi-ripe dragon fruit.

About Subko VLGE: Co-operative Agriculture

A sustainable, farm-to-table-to-farmer operation by Subko

Founded by Subko Specialty Coffee Roasters and Craft Bakehouse, the Subko Co-op initiative finds its roots in the village of K. Thadiputtu in Andhra Pradesh. Concentrating its efforts on the holistic advancement of the 'Subko Village,' Subko Co-op has adopted a cluster comprising six tribal farmers from K. Thadiputtu village in Paderu, Andhra Pradesh. With a dedication to bringing these individuals to the forefront of the third wave of coffee, Subko Co-op seeks to not only empower these farmers but to also nurture growth within their entire community.

This initiative is focused on tribal farmers who cultivate coffee on government-allotted lands. With an attention on driving direct trade, sustainability, and hyper-traceability, the initiative embodies a commitment to elevating the agricultural landscape in the world of coffee. This endeavor aims to adopt more such clusters in the future. Furthermore, Subko Co-op envisions the establishment of training centers, designed to empower and educate both farmers and their families, paving the way for them to become coffee professionals and authentic representatives of their cultural legacy and heritage. Subko Co-op’s objective is to emerge as a transformative force, reshaping the narrative of coffee cultivation by amalgamating sustainable practices, cultural preservation, and community empowerment, and to narrate origin stories and recognise every stakeholder who puts their heart in coffee cultivation.

name: Let's Chocolate [Pan-India]
description:
A photobook made in collaboration with photographer Rid Burman and multidisciplinary artist Aniruddh Mehta.

Photographed in this book are the humans who construct the infrastructure & assemble machines that are required for an artisan chocolate factory to exist.
A raw, unfiltered book with honest faces; and messy too.

Pages : 38 Pages Incl. Cover
Close Size : 7.72" (W) x 9.88"
(H)

About the Artists

Rid Burman

Rid Burman is a photographer born in India in the early 80s. He has his roots in a family of sculptors and painters. Naturally, art has always been a priority in Burman's approach to photography. After graduating from the Brooks Institute of Photography in California in 2000, Burman moved to New York and worked as an assistant for Steven Klein and Mark Seliger. He returned to India in 2008 and started collaborating with with prestigious brands, also with magazines such as Elle and Vogue to name a very few. He has a certain propensity to create unique stories and a vision of his own. Always on the move, Burman works between Paris, New York and Mumbai, constantly exploring new ideas, new places, drawing on the abundant inspirations of his Eastern and Western philosophies.

Aniruddh Mehta

Aniruddh Mehta is an Artist and a Designer based in Mumbai, India. His work ranges from traditional graphic design as well as digital and new media arts. His practices traverse through various mediums with a common theme rooted in precise organization.

He is the founder of Studio Bigfat - a multi-disciplinary design studio focusing on a broad spectrum of design areas such as Branding, Packaging, Brand Strategy, Graphic Design, Digital Illustration and Motion Design. The studio has worked with a long list of clientele; some of which includes Facebook, Puma, Apple, Gates Foundation, LVMH, Subko Coffee, etc.

name: Excelsa community
description:
We hand-pick fully ripe, deep red cherries with high sugar content, ensuring minimal defects and consistent quality. After harvesting, cherries are sorted in water; ripe cherries sink while underripe or damaged ones float and are removed. 
Sorted cherries are spread in thin layers on raised beds in a ventilated polyhouse, which controls temperature and protects against rain and UV exposure. We turn the cherries manually to ensure even drying and prevent fermentation. Regular raking promotes airflow, enhancing the final flavor.
In the evenings, cherries are covered to shield them from moisture. We monitor moisture levels, aiming for 11–12% to preserve flavors and minimize microbial risks. After drying, cherries are packed in jute sacks and stored for at least two months to stabilize and mature.

The Mooleh Manay estate is situated near the scenic backwaters of the Harangi Reservoir in Coorg, Karnataka. It employs a data-oriented strategy for farming and coffee processing, as it believes that data plays a crucial role in enhancing agricultural practices and achieving top-quality coffee production. The estate grows various coffee types, such as Arabica, Robusta, and Excelsa, and utilizes careful processing techniques to highlight the finest flavors. The estate is dedicated to ongoing improvement and innovation and engages in research focused on indigenous Indian Coffea species and soil health.

name: Raxidi Naturals
description:
After selective picking of the best coffee cherries, the cherries were washed and kept in a stainless steel container. We used a strain called W1 which is a mix of yeast and bacteria to ferment the cherries for 48 hours in an anaerobic condition. After which they were removed and taken to raised beds for slow drying for 21 days. In the drying yard a controlled environment was maintained accounting for temperature and humidity which was monitored regularly.

Raxidi Estate, located at an elevation of 950-1000 meters in Sakleshpur, Karnataka, spans 165 acres and has been nurtured by three generations of the Lobo family since the 1950s. Currently, father-daughter duo Richard and Rachel Lobo continue this legacy, cultivating Arabica varieties such as Selection 6, Catimore, and Chandragiri, alongside Robusta varieties like old Peredenia and Selection 270. Their focus on micro-lots and innovative processing techniques results in coffee with unique depth and character, with every step, from handpicking cherries to using pure spring water, executed with precision.

name: 84 Hours Anoxic Naturals
description:
Coffee cherries are hand picked at their peak ripeness to ensure high quality beans. The outer skin is removed using a depulping machine, leaving beans covered in mucilage. Unlike traditional methods, fermentation occurs in oxygen free tanks. The beans ferment in these sealed tanks for about 84 hours, which influences their flavor and aroma. After fermentation, the mucilage remains as the beans are dried on raised beds or patios under controlled conditions for even drying.

Located in Chikmagalur, Sai Ashirwad estate is renowned for growing various coffees, including Arabica SLN 795,CxR and Robusta Old Peridenia. The farm has organic certification, showcasing its commitment to sustainable practices. Beyond coffee, it is a haven for wildlife like Indian Gaur and Malabar Giant squirrels. The estate features its own processing unit and drying yards to ensure careful handling of beans. Additionally, water harvesting ponds reflect their focus on environmental stewardship.

name: Kenyan Washed
description: After harvesting, ripe coffee cherries are brought to the factory by smallholder farmers for wet processing, where the skin and pulp are removed. This process relies on electrical pumps to bring water from the nearest source into reservoir tanks. To conserve water, the factory recirculates it during processing. A disc pulper with three sets of discs is used to separate the skin and fruit from the green coffee beans. Following pulping, the coffee ferments overnight to break down sugars, then it is cleaned, soaked, and spread on raised drying tables. The drying time varies based on climate conditions and the volume of coffee being processed.

The beans were then dried on raised beds under the mountain sun, allowing for gradual moisture stabilisation. This double-washed method produces a cup that is bold, clear, and refreshingly juicy.

This unique method really brings out the coffee's natural sweetness and clarity, making every sip a delightful tasting adventure. You'll get to enjoy a lovely tropical mix of flavors, including Pear, Green Apple Candy, and Blackberries. It's all about creating a fun and flavorful experience in your cup!

name: Culture Process
description: This exceptional coffee undergoes an 72-hour CULTURE PROCESS, sourced from the Catuai varietal at our farm, located 4,400 feet high in the Jeri Patte block. After harvesting with a Brix of 25.8, we placed the cherries in stainless-steel fermenters, adding a specific strain of yeast and lactic acid bacteria. The fermentation took place in a carbon dioxide-rich environment, followed by a slow drying process on raised beds over 29 days with constant stirring. This meticulous approach enhances the unique flavor profile of our coffee.

name: Ārabhi
description:
Our smash hit organic arabica is back with even more complexity this season! 

Grown and processed at the extremely biodiverse Narmada estate, Chikmagalur; this certified organic arabica has gone through a closely monitored wet ferment for 36 hours post pulping. Afterwards, the coffee is washed thoroughly to remove the left over mucilage and dried slowly. 

 The result of this careful processing is a delightfully complex cup that brims with a very distinct acidity that reminds us of apricot and passion fruit. This is wonderfully balanced with a praline-esque like nuttiness and reminds or roaster of the rāga ārabhi.

Ārabhi the coffee is a delight across all manual brews 8 days post date of roast. It also makes for a crisp espresso shot 18 days post date of roast.

We thank South India coffee company for introducing us to this hidden gem and we hope to continue working with them for years to come!

name: Mind = Blown
description:
OG best seller is back again and this time it's a light roast! 

 The good folks at Mooleh Manay wanted to improve upon last season's outcome by adding a little more complexity without losing on the sweetness and not adding much funk. They have made small tweaks to their processing and it has worked wonders in the cup!

 The start of the  process is by picking ripe arabica cherries(mix of Sln6, Sln 9 and Chandragiri) and using a syphon tank to remove immature cherries that float.

 The sunken cherries are then pre dried. This is a very important step as it reduces the moisture, which helps achieve better control in the fermentation. This goes a long way to prevent any off flavours.

 The pre-dried cherries are then put in sealed barrels , inoculated with a custom yeast culture and a controlled carbonic maceration enviornment is created. The fermentation lasts for 60 hours.

 The cherries are then dried in a poly house for 10 days, where they are raked constantly to ensure even drying.

 This intricate process has resulted in a coffee that is a revelation! We tried a lot of different  roasts for this coffee and ultimately settled on a light roast that amps up the acidity and brings the complexity front and centre. We taste very prominent banana and raspberry  in the acidity that is balanced really well with a vanilla-eque sweetness. This coffee is a real  delight on a manual brew(we prefer a v60) with really vibrant  acidity, great sweetness and next to no bitterness even when extraction is pushed.

 The coffee really opens up 12 days post roast date for manual brews and makes for a fruit jam of an espresso 20 days post roast date. This coffee is not be missed on any count!

name: Pūrnashadjam
description:
The smash hit robusta from last season is back with a bang! We are very pleased at how last season's iteration of this coffee turned out and this year is even better.

 The good folks at Mooleh Manay have thrown the kitchen sink at processing their robusta with the aim of making it delightful in the cup and boy have they delivered!

For this lot, ripe C×R cherries are floated to remove defects and then fermented in sealed pressurised  barrels and inoculated with a custom cluture for 168 hours (yes you read that right!). The combination of pressure from the CO2 and the custom culture ensures proper breakdown of the mucilage. The cherries are then slow dried on raised beds to stabilise  water activity.

 The result of all this care is a cup that has none of the harshness that is usually associated with robusta. We have infact  roasted this coffee to medium as it would be a crime to mask the complexity with a darker roast! 

All our test roasts were smooth, sweet , fruity and faintly winey! We taste a pleasant sweetness and nuttiness that reminds us of raisins and biscotti. The blueberry like fruitiness present in the aroma shows up towards the end especially as the cup cools along with a pleasant wine like after taste. We liked how soft and elegant this robusta  tasted last season and this season is no different. The elegance of this coffee reminded us of the rāga pūrnashadjam (which is a slightly rare but has oodles of consonance).

 Pūrnashadjam the coffee makes for a delightful manual brew (we prefer a 16.5 g dose for 300g water to deal with the extra caffeine) on a v60 7 days post roast and makes for sweet sweet shot of Crema laden espresso 18 days from date of roast.
