name: Tōdi
description:
Our bold dark roast is back!

Sourced from Krishnagiri estate ,high up in the Chandra drona hills(a.k.a the Giris) of Chikmagalur, this lot of washed arabica fascinated us with its bean density and versatility(traits we have come to associate with the coffee from Krishnagiri estate).

Ripe cherries of the Chandrigiri varietal have been selected for this lot and the estate has tweaked their standard washed process to eke more out of the coffee.

Just like last year, we decided to a more developed roast apart from the medium roast; taking the beans close to second crack but stopping short of that that point. This makes the coffee stand up to milk better but retains some origin character which manifests this year and faint raspberry like fruitiness

The boldness of this coffee reminds us of the rāga tōdi and is our go to for milk based drinks.

Tōdi the coffee is a delight on the espresso machine14 days post date of roast and also works very well for  moka pot , south-indian filter and immersion brewers like French press and Aeropress.

name: Nalinakānti
description:
Last season's hit from Ram estate is back!

Located in the village of Kamanur near Thandigudi, Ram estate (called Rothaikadu by locals ) posseses a unique microclimate that is idealfor growing complex arabicas  and the folks there  have been processing top notch coffees from year one of their foray into the  speciality scene.

  This particular lot consists only of  selectively picked SLN 09 arabica from the estate's highest portion. We had a hand in fine tuning the processing this lot and we thank Ram estate for listening to our suggestions. While the total fermentation time was 160 hrs, this was split between pre and post pulping. The cherries were fermented in a steel barrel with CO2 being pumped in. They were then taken out, pulped and then fermented again in similar conditionstill a total time of 160 hrs was reached. 

  The resulting cup is very aromatic ,very  tropical  and very sweet, but also shockingly 'clean' tasting ; without much fermenty notes. This is party a result of the aforementioned microclimate and partly because of careful monitoring of the cherries during fermentation and the slow drying.  The acidity tastes of lychee with a lingering raisin like sweetness and a subtle rosewater undercurrent which we find very refreshing, like the rāga nalinakānti.

Nalinakānti the coffee is a very sweet , complex, sippable brew  and is a delight across all manual brew methods 10 days post roasting. It makes a fruity shot of espresso 20 days post date of roast.

name: Hamsanādam
description:
We have a new washed coffee and it's a revelation!

 Perumpallam is a village on the northern  side of the lower Kodaikanal hills. The high altitude of the place is very conducive for growing complex arabicas. 

We have been fascinated by how complex the Kodaikanal region is as a coffee growing area and have been especially curious about  the higher elevation small holder farms there.

 The good folks at Ram estate helped us procure this interesting community arabica lot from Perumpallam. The varietal is chandragiri and the processing is a simple traditional washed. This simplicity allows the plant care and the terroir to really shine in the cup.

 We took our time dialling in the roast of this lot but once we figured out a profile that worked, the cup really started to shine. There is oodles of milk chocolate sweetness that is punctuated by a lemon candy like acidity and marigold florals. The coffee does take some time to peak but once there we also started noticing raspberry like fruitiness too!  This complex effervescence reminded our roaster of the rāga hamsanādam.

Hamsanādam the coffee is a delight across all manual brews but especially the v60 , 12 days post date of roast. It also makes for a more-ish shot of espresso 24 days post date of roast! We hope to source more frequently from this high altitude corner of the Kodaikanal hills!

Coffee Variety - Arabica Beans
Post-Harvest Process - Red Honey sun-dried 
Roast Level - Dark Roast
Region - Chikmagalur, Karnataka 

Balur Estate, a 250-acre single estate in the Western Ghats, is managed by third-generation planters. Established during British rule, it practices sustainable farming without external fertilisers or pesticides. In addition to coffee, it produces nutmeg, cacao, citrus fruits, and jackfruit. A serene lake supports its diverse crops. Nestled in a UNESCO World Heritage site, the estate thrives in harmony with nature, reflecting local traditions of respect and coexistence.

name: Kolli Berry Estate
description:
Coffee Variety - Arabica Beans 
Post Harvest Process - Washed
Roast level - Medium Roast 
Region - Mudigere, Chikmagalur

Kolli Berri Estate in Mudigere, 30 km from Chikmagalur, a women-led enterprise run by Pranathi Shetty. The cup is clean, uniform, and marked by bold flavors that cut through with clarity and balance. Designed for everyday drinking, it carries both strength and refinement - dependable yet distinctive.

The coffee starts with a comforting malt-like aroma. In the cup, notes of dark chocolate take center stage, followed by hints of ripe prunes that add depth and sweetness. A gentle acidity brings brightness, while the rounded body creates a smooth and satisfying mouthfeel. Clean and well-structured, the cup showcases consistency from start to finish, ending with delicate traces of cocoa and dried fruit.

The coffee cherries were harvested at peak ripeness from farms located between 3,500 and 3,750 feet above sea level. After harvest, the cherries were carefully sorted, with all floaters and defective fruit removed before pulping. The parchment coffee was then fermented to break down the remaining mucilage, washed thoroughly, and slowly dried. This careful washed process helps preserve the coffee's sweetness, clarity, and uniform character in the final cup.

It reminds us of :
Whole Beans - Prunes, Dark Chocolate, Malt, Medium Acidity, Full Body.
French Press - Hazelnut, Hints of Cinnamon, Prune, Medium Acidity, Full Body.
Pour Over - Pineapple, Dried Apricots, Hint of Dark Chocolate, Low Acidity, Medium Body.
Mokapot / Percolator - Malt, Milk chocolate, Roasted Peanuts, Medium Acidity, Full Body.
Espresso - Cacao Bitters, Dried Apricot, Medium Acidity, Full Body.
Aeropress - Pomegranate, Oranges, Grapefruit, Low Acidity, Medium Body.

name: Nicobar Brew Bags (Set of 5)
description:
Created in collaboration with Nicobar, this special edition pays tribute to the remarkable journey of coffee to India. From Yemen to the hills of Chikmagalur, the packaging reimagines this story through Nicobar's signature lens of travel, culture and thoughtful design. The illustrated artwork traces the routes, landscapes and encounters that shaped coffee's passage across continents, celebrating the spirit of exploration that continues to connect people through a shared love for coffee. Paired with Bili Hu's specialty Arabica coffee, this collaboration brings together two brands united by a passion for craftsmanship, storytelling, and meaningful experiences. Our Drip Coffee Bags are a blend of Arabica Beans sourced from two distinct plantations in Chikmagalur, Karnataka. Through a process of washing and pulping, these sundried Arabicas unite to deliver a naturally sweet, berry-like flavor profile, harmonizing the bold body and bitterness of the brew. Whether brewed hot, cold or with milk, indulge in its rich taste.

1. Crafted entirely from Chikmagalur, Karnataka's coffee offerings.
2. Each sachet caters to a single-cup serving.
3. Travel Friendly
4. Each brew bag is 11g each Brewing your favorite cup has never been simpler, here’s how to brew:

• Tear open the bag at the top.
• Gently shake to ensure even distribution and place the hanger securely over the cup.
• Slowly pour hot water into the bag until it reaches the neck.
• Refill with more water once the filtration process completes.
• Cease pouring when the brewed coffee level in the cup reaches midway through the filter.
• Discard the used filter and serve.
• Brewing time: under 2 minutes.
• Total hot water required: 200ml

name: Black Honey Vienna Roast
description:
Coffee Variety - SLN 13 Arabica Beans 
Post Harvest Process - 720 hours Extended Fermentation, Black Honey Sun Dried Arabicas
Roast level - Vienna Dark Roast 
Region - Kalledevarapura Estate, Bababudangiri, Chikmagalur

This experimental coffee undergoes an extended 30-day fermentation process in controlled fermentation VATS, designed to push the boundaries of flavour development and create an intensely funky, wine-forward profile.

Following fermentation, the cherries are carefully sun-dried for 10 days before being rested and aged as green coffee for over 8 months, allowing the flavours to deepen and mature beautifully.

Roasted specifically as a vienna dark roast, this coffee delivers a bold and decadent cup with reduced acidity and a rich, creamy body. Expect notes of dark chocolate, cocoa bitters, spiced rum, caramelised sweetness, and a lingering peppery spice finish.

name: Wild Fig Co-Ferment
description:
Coffee Variety - Chandragiri Arabica Beans 
Post Harvest Process - Wild Fig Co-Ferment, Washed Arabica
Roast level - Medium Roast 
Region - Kalledevarapura Estate, Bababudangiri, Chikmagalur

Some ideas begin not in the lab or the market — but underfoot.

This micro-lot was born not out of invention, but observation. One morning walk, somewhere between the canopy and the soil, a whisper of possibility stirred. Wild figs - soft, fallen, sticky-sweet, scattered the forest floor like little forgotten gifts. Not harvested. Not sold. Just there. Fermenting into the earth.

In that moment, something shifted. What if the forest had already done half the work? What if nature, in her quiet generosity, had left behind an ingredient that was both abundant and invisible, until you slowed down enough to see it?

This is that coffee. Grown under the shade of fig trees. Fermented not with fuss or fanfare, but with what was already given. The cup that emerged is rich, round, and quietly wild.

Roasted to a medium profile to coax out depth without losing nuance, this coffee opens boozy and heady, rum and raisins layered with brown sugar and dried berries. A hum of fermented fig threads through it all, grounding the cup.

It reminds us of :
Whole Beans - Rum & Raisins, Brown Sugar & Dried Berries Medium Acidity, Full Body
French Press - Caramelized Honey, Winey & Apricot, Medium  Acidity, Medium Body 
Pour Over - Rose, Raspberry, Lime, Medium Acidity, Medium Body 
Mokapot / Percolator - Winey, Dried Berries, Roasted Nuts Medium Acidity, Full Body 
Espresso - Roasted Almonds, Peach & Apricot, Medium Acidity, Medium Body 
Aeropress - Nutmeg, Black Grapes, Medium Acidity, Full Body

name: Monsooned Malabar
description:
Coffee Variety - AA Arabica Beans
Post-Harvest Process - Unwashed, Monsooned 
Roast Level - Medium - Light Roast
Region - Chikmagalur, Karnataka

Monsooned Malabar - A Unique Specialty Coffee from India.

The arabica beans from Chikmagalur are transported to Mangalore, a coastal city in India. During the monsoon season, the beans absorb moisture from the coastal winds, causing them to swell and develop a pale yellow color. This process results in some of the most distinctive flavors found in coffee. This unique Indian practice has gained global recognition, and we are delighted to offer it to discerning coffee lovers in India. Ideal for manual extraction methods and is enjoyed best as black coffee.

name: Whiskey Barrel Aged Brew Bags, Medium Roast (Set of 5)
description:
Brewed effortlessly in your drip bag, best enjoyed black.

Our Barrel-Aged Coffee begins Its journey with green coffee beans patiently aged in upcycled whiskey barrels for three weeks. During this time, the beans naturally absorb the rich, aromatic essence of the barrels, infusing them with deep, complex flavors reminiscent of Irish cream—silky, smooth, and laced with subtle notes of vanilla and oak. 

Once the beans reach their peak infusion, they are carefully roasted to enhance their unique character, creating a harmonious blend of creamy, whiskey-like undertones with the boldness of perfectly roasted coffee.

The entire process is completely natural, leaving no trace of alcohol while delivering an exceptional coffee experience that’s as rich in flavor as it is sustainable. Perfect for those who crave something daringly different in their cup!
Disclaimer "It does not contain alcohol"

  1. Each sachet caters to a single-cup serving.
  2. Travel Friendly
  3. Net weight: 55grams (5 sachets x 11g each)

Brewing your favorite cup has never been simpler:

  • Tear open the bag at the top.
  • Gently shake to ensure even distribution and place the hanger securely over the cup.
  • Slowly pour hot water into the bag until it reaches the neck.
  • Refill with more water once the filtration process completes.
  • Cease pouring when the brewed coffee level in the cup reaches midway through the filter.
  • Discard the used filter and serve.
  • Brewing time: under 2 minutes.
  • Total hot water required: 200ml.

name: Assorted Drip Coffee Bags (Set of 5)
description:
Our Assorted Drip Coffee Box, a thoughtfully curated collection of single-serve drip coffee sachets for effortless brewing, unique and exceptional flavors. Each box brings together distinctive coffees from different origins, roast profiles, and processing styles - perfect for gifting, or daily indulgence.

Inside, you will find a balanced mix of
- Arabica Medium Roast with smooth, rounded notes
- Arabica Dark Roast delivering bold intensity and depth
- The iconic Monsooned Malabar, known for its low acidity and earthy richness
- Our indulgent Whiskey Barrel Aged Coffee, infused with warm, oaky character
- Decaffeinated coffee, offering full-bodied flavor with less caffeine.

Each sachet is individually packed to preserve freshness and flavor, allowing you to enjoy coffee anywhere, with no machine required. Whether you’re a seasoned coffee lover or just beginning your journey, this assorted box celebrates variety, craftsmanship, and the joy of discovering something new in every cup.

How to brew? 

  • Tear open the bag at the top.
  • Gently shake to ensure even distribution and place the hanger securely over the cup.
  • Slowly pour hot water into the bag until it reaches the neck.
  • Refill with more water once the filtration process completes.
  • Cease pouring when the brewed coffee level in the cup reaches midway through the filter.
  • Discard the used filter and serve.
  • Brewing time: under 2 minutes.
  • Total hot water required: 200ml.

name: Whiskey Barrel Aged Coffee
description:
Coffee Variety - Arabica Beans
Post-Harvest Process - Washed
Roast Level - Medium Roast
Region - Chikmagalur, Karnataka  

Our Barrel-Aged Coffee begins Its journey with green coffee beans patiently aged in upcycled whiskey barrels for three weeks. During this time, the beans naturally absorb the rich, aromatic essence of the barrels, infusing them with deep, complex flavors reminiscent of Irish cream—silky, smooth, and laced with subtle notes of vanilla and oak. 

Once the beans reach their peak infusion, they are carefully roasted to enhance their unique character, creating a harmonious blend of creamy, whiskey-like undertones with the boldness of perfectly roasted coffee.

The entire process is completely natural, leaving no trace of alcohol while delivering an exceptional coffee experience that’s as rich in flavor as it is sustainable. Perfect for those who crave something daringly different in their cup! Disclaimer "It does not contain alcohol"

It reminds us of :

Whole Beans - Irish Cream, Single Malt, Green Apple, Medium Acidity, Full Body
Cold Brew - Irish Whiskey, Hints of Oak and Vanilla, Medium Acidity, Medium Body

name: Hot Coffee Dip Bags
description:
Elevate your coffee ritual with our Hot Coffee Dip Bags, delivering convenience without compromising on quality or flavor.

Our dip bags consist of Arabica and Robusta blend, sourced from the finest coffee plantations from Chikmagalur, Karnataka. Each sachet ensures a rich, aromatic experience that's perfect for one cup.

  • Your travel buddy.
  • All you need is a cup and hot water. No brewing equipment is required. 
  • Brew it anywhere you like. 
  • Each sachet serves one cup.
  • Net weight: 45 grams (9g x 5 sachets).

  • Pour 200ml of hot water over the bag.
  • Dunk the bag for 15-30 seconds to enhance extraction.
  • Allow the bag to steep in the cup for 5 minutes or longer, tailoring the strength to suit your taste preferences.

name: Hot Coffee Drip Bags, Medium Roast
description:
Our Drip Bags are a blend of Arabica Coffee Beans sourced from two distinct plantations in Chikmagalur, Karnataka. Through a process of washing and pulping, these sundried Arabicas unite to deliver a naturally sweet, berry-like flavor profile, harmonizing the bold body and bitterness of the brew. Whether brewed hot, cold or with milk, indulge in its rich taste.

  1. Crafted entirely from Chikmagalur, Karnataka's coffee offerings.
  2. Each sachet caters to a single-cup serving.
  3. Travel Friendly 
  4. Each brew bag is 11g each

Brewing your favorite cup has never been simpler:

  • Tear open the bag at the top.
  • Gently shake to ensure even distribution and place the hanger securely over the cup.
  • Slowly pour hot water into the bag until it reaches the neck.
  • Refill with more water once the filtration process completes.
  • Cease pouring when the brewed coffee level in the cup reaches midway through the filter.
  • Discard the used filter and serve.
  • Brewing time: under 2 minutes.
  • Total hot water required: 200ml.

name: Cold Brew Blend
description:
Less Bitter, Smoother, Chocolaty, have it chilled!

A blend of Arabica and Robusta coffee beans sourced from plantations of Chikmagalur. Our cold brew blend which is roasted medium is specially designed to extract a full-bodied, flavorful, and low acidity when brewed cold. Once brewed, it will remind you of Dark Chocolate and a hint of caramel.

How to brew?

1. Take 100 grams of ground coffee and mix it with 1 ltr of cold water in an open container. Cover and let it sit undisturbed for 16-18 hours.
2. Filter the brew in a bottle or jar using a muslin cloth or cold brew filter paper.
3. Store the filtered coffee in the refrigerator. Consume within 7-10 days for optimal freshness.
4. When serving, add ice cubes, milk, and sweetener according to your preference.

name: SCA COURSES
description:
SCA Brewing Foundation Course

The Brewing Foundation course offers a comprehensive introduction to the art and science of coffee brewing. Through both theory and hands-on practice, learners are guided through various brewing methods using a range of devices.

This course is ideal for beginners and provides the fundamental skills and knowledge needed to craft delicious brewed coffee. 

What You'll Learn: 
1. Coffee Knowledge : Understand Arabica vs. Robusta, processing methods, and best practices for coffee storage.
2. Brewing Methods & Equipment : Explore manual brewers like V60, French Press, and AeroPress, and learn how to use essential brewing tools.
3. Brewing Guidelines : Master the 7 key elements of brewing: ratio, grind, time, temperature, turbulence, water quality, and filter type.
4. Brewing Techniques : Practice percolation (V60), immersion (French Press), and hybrid (AeroPress) brewing styles.
5. Brew Analysis : Learn to evaluate your brew by analyzing its color, aroma, taste, and body.
6. Equipment Maintenance : Maintain your brewing tools for consistency, cleanliness, and long-term performance.

Certification:
Upon successful completion of both the practical and theoretical exams, participants will receive the SCA Brewing Foundation Certificate.

SCA Brewing Intermediate Course

Take the next step in your coffee journey with the SCA Brewing Intermediate course at Corridor Seven Coffee Roasters. This intensive 2-day course is designed for experienced brewers and coffee enthusiasts ready to master their craft and earn an internationally recognized certification.

Perfect for anyone who has completed the Foundation course, this program goes beyond the basics to deepen your understanding of the science and art of brewing. You will gain advanced coffee brewing skills through a mix of theory and hands-on practice, empowering you to consistently produce exceptional coffee.

What You'll Learn
Our comprehensive coffee brewing course covers essential topics to help you elevate your brews:

1. Advanced Brewing Principles: Learn the key variables that influence brew strength and coffee extraction for ultimate cup quality.
2. Sensory Analysis: Develop your coffee sensory skills to evaluate brews, assessing aroma, taste, body, and flavor with confidence.
3. Controlling Variables: Master the impact of grind size, brewing time, water temperature, and turbulence on your coffee.
4. Expert Techniques: Identify and correct common issues like under, over, and uneven extraction.
5. Roast Level & Water Chemistry: Understand the effect of roast level and the crucial role of water chemistry on flavor.
6. Professional Tools: Get hands-on with tools used to measure soluble concentration and calculate extraction yield.

Certification:
Upon successful completion of the in-person practical exam and the online written exam, you will receive your official SCA Brewing Intermediate Certificate. This credential is an industry standard for professional brewers and a significant step in your coffee education journey.

SCA Brewing Professional Course

The SCA Brewing Professional course is where science meets mastery. Designed for those who have completed the SCA Brewing Intermediate level, this advanced program takes you deep into the chemistry, physics, and sensory dimensions of coffee brewing. Over 21 hours (3 days) of focused learning, you’ll sharpen your analytical skills, refine your brewing precision, and earn an internationally recognized certification that sets you apart in the world of specialty coffee.

    • Required: SCA Brewing Intermediate

  • Exams: Written and Practical 

  • Time: 10:00 AM – 7:30 PM (including breaks) (3 days)

  • Course Fee: INR 53,100 (inclusive of GST)

Your course fee covers all professional brewing equipment, study materials, and access to your SCA certification exams.

What You’ll Learn

The Brewing Professional course builds on prior knowledge and takes you into the heart of brewing science:
1. Advanced Coffee Knowledge
Understand how roast level influences extraction, flavor, and sensory perception.

2. Brewing Methods & Equipment
Explore how device shapes, bed depth, and filter media affect brewing outcomes. Learn how to select, calibrate, and optimize gravity brewers for precision brewing.

3. Brewing Guidelines
Dive into the 7 Essential Elements of Brewing and master the relationships between grind size, particle distribution, brewing time, temperature, and turbulence.

4. Water Chemistry & Quality
Gain an expert understanding of water’s origin, hardness, alkalinity, and treatment methods. Learn to test and modify water composition to bring out the best in your coffee.

5. Brewing Process
Analyze each brewing phase from wetting and blooming to extraction and yield calculation while understanding how these affect sensory results.

6. Brew Analysis & Sensory Evaluation
Measure soluble yield and concentration, describe a balanced brew, and use professional tools to interpret data and sensory feedback accurately.

7. Maintenance & Optimization
Learn how grinder burr quality and replacement cycles affect consistency, and explore the sensory and technical impact of bypass brewing techniques.

Certification: Upon successful completion, you’ll receive the SCA Brewing Professional Certificate, recognized globally as the standard for professional coffee brewers.

name: Salawara Estate Pichia Fermentation HSD
description:
• Tastes Like - Green Apple, Prune and Creamy Mouthfeel 
  • Roasting Profile - Filter ( Light Roast )
  • Process -  Honey Sun Dried
  • Varietal - SL 6 + SL 9
  • Altitude - 1050 MASL
  • Producer Name - Mr. Sharan Gowda
  • Harvest Year - 2024-2025

Coffee Producers Note -
The coffees were harvested from Block 24 at a Brix level of 22. This lot underwent yeast inoculation using Pichia and Lactobacillus, fermented in large stainless-steel tanks. Carbon dioxide was introduced during fermentation to enhance the coffee’s fruity flavour profile. The coffee was then processed using the natural method and slow-dried for 22 days in a controlled nursery drying system.

Roasters Note - 
This lot shows a bright green-apple acidity layered over prune-like sweetness. We roasted it to keep those fruit tones intact while allowing the creamy mouthfeel to carry through on the finish. Development was kept controlled to retain clarity and balance without compromising texture, making it suited for both filter and modern espresso styles.

name: Salawara Estate Mosto fermentation
description:
• Tastes Like - White peach, Golden Raisin and Bergamot
  • Roasting Profile - Filter ( Light Roast )
  • Process -  Champagne Fermentation
  • Varietal - SL 795
  • Altitude - 1050 MASL
  • Producer Name - Mr. Sharan Gowda
  • Harvest Year - 2024-2025

Coffee Producers Note -
“Mosto” refers to the sweet, fermented juice extracted from coffee cherries or their mucilage, rich in natural sugars, acids, and a diverse microbial culture of yeasts and bacteria. Fresh coffee cherries are placed in large, food-grade barrels, and “musto” from a previous batch of natural coffees is added to accelerate fermentation and enhance complexity. The coffees are then slow-dried using a nursery-style drying method.

Roasters Note - 
In the cup, expect a delicate interplay of white peach and golden raisin, bringing a soft, rounded sweetness, while bergamot lifts the profile with a fragrant, citrusy brightness. The acidity is elegant with a silky mouthfeel and a clean, lingering finish. The nursery-style drying further refines the structure of the cup, preserving aromatics while enhancing sweetness and balance.
A refined and aromatic profile. ideal for those who enjoy floral, fruit-forward coffees with a composed fermentation character.

name: SCA Brewing Intermediate Course
description:
Take the next step in your coffee journey with the SCA Brewing Intermediate course at Corridor Seven Coffee Roasters. This intensive 2-day course is designed for experienced brewers and coffee enthusiasts ready to master their craft and earn an internationally recognized certification.

Perfect for anyone who has completed the Foundation course, this program goes beyond the basics to deepen your understanding of the science and art of brewing. You will gain advanced coffee brewing skills through a mix of theory and hands-on practice, empowering you to consistently produce exceptional coffee.

What You'll Learn

Our comprehensive coffee brewing course covers essential topics to help you elevate your brews:

  • Advanced Brewing Principles: Learn the key variables that influence brew strength and coffee extraction for ultimate cup quality.

  • Sensory Analysis: Develop your coffee sensory skills to evaluate brews, assessing aroma, taste, body, and flavor with confidence.

  • Controlling Variables: Master the impact of grind size, brewing time, water temperature, and turbulence on your coffee.

  • Expert Techniques: Identify and correct common issues like under, over, and uneven extraction.

  • Roast Level & Water Chemistry: Understand the effect of roast level and the crucial role of water chemistry on flavor.

  • Professional Tools: Get hands-on with tools used to measure soluble concentration and calculate extraction yield.

About Your Certified SCA Trainer

This course is led by Naitik Shah, a certified SCA Authorized Trainer (AST) and the head of the coffee program at Corridor Seven Coffee Roasters. Naitik brings a wealth of hands-on experience in brewing, sensory analysis, and the broader specialty coffee industry. His expertise ensures you receive a solid foundation that blends global standards with real-world insights, preparing you for the SCA Coffee Courses.

Course Details & Outcomes

Upon successful completion of the in-person practical exam and the online written exam, you will receive your official SCA Brewing Intermediate Certificate. This credential is an industry standard for professional brewers and a significant step in your coffee education journey.

  • Course Fee: INR 37,760 (inclusive of GST)

  • Time: 10:30 AM - 6:30 PM

Your course fee includes access to all comprehensive materials, professional brewing equipment, and your SCA certificate upon successful completion.

Ready to take your brewing skills to the next level? Contact us today to secure your spot in this exclusive course.

name: Melkodige Estate Saccharomyces 72hrs Naturals
description:
• Tastes Like - Pomegranate, Pink Guava and Golden Raisins
  • Roasting Profile - Filter ( Light Roast )
  • Process -  Saccharomyces 72hrs Naturals
  • Varietal - Sl 9
  • Altitude - 1280 MASL  
  • Producer Name - Aveen and Yogita Rodrigues 
  • Harvest Year - 2025

Coffee Producers Note -
Red, fully ripe cherries with a Brix level above 22 are selectively handpicked and carefully cleaned using a water bath to remove impurities and lighter fruit. The cherries then undergo anaerobic fermentation in sealed drums for 72 hours, allowing complex flavours to develop.

Post-fermentation, they are transferred to raised wooden drying beds and dried slowly under shade nets. During this stage, the cherries are regularly raked to ensure even and consistent drying. Once fully dried, they are packed into gunny bags and rested for 60 days, allowing the flavours to stabilise and mature before further processing.

Roasters Note -
We’ve taken this coffee light to preserve its vibrancy and showcase the fruit character developed during fermentation. Expect a bright, expressive cup with juicy acidity and a clean, lingering sweetness.
In the cup:
Pomegranate leads with a fresh, winey brightness, followed by soft pink guava and a rounded golden raisin sweetness on the finish. The body is smooth and supple, with a crisp yet balanced aftertaste.
Best enjoyed when brewed clean and slightly cooler to let the fruit open up gradually.

description:

name: Latte Art: Pour and Practice
description:
Unleash your inner barista and transform your coffee into a canvas! This immersive "Latte Art: Pour and Practice" workshop is designed for coffee enthusiasts of all skill levels, from beginners eager to pour their first heart to seasoned home baristas looking to refine their craft.

Date & Time: 11th NOV 2025 | 12 PM - 1 PM

Location: Corridor Seven Coffee Academy [Map Link]

What You'll Learn:

  • Milk Steaming: Create silky microfoam.

  • Pouring Techniques: Understand the physics and technique behind a controlled pour.

  • Basic Latte Art: Learn to craft hearts, rosettas, and tulips.

  • Expert Tips & Practice: Get personalized feedback and refine your skills.

By the end of this workshop, you'll not only be pouring beautiful latte art but also understanding the nuances that contribute to an exceptional coffee experience. Elevate your daily brew and impress your friends with your newfound skills!

name: Champion’s Table – Coffee Omakase Experience
description:
The Champion’s Table is Mithilesh Vazalwar’s way of bringing his first-round World Championship journey back to his hometown.

Each seat becomes part of a story techniques honed on the global stage, flavors shaped by travel, and the spirit of Corridor Seven Coffee now reaching across borders.

This isn’t just about tasting coffee. It’s about immersing yourself in the craft, the precision, and the vision that placed an Indian roaster among the world’s best.

With only 9 seats, the atmosphere is intimate, the experience is personal, and the brews unlike anything you’ve experienced before.

description:
The French Press is a low tech portable coffee brewing method. Let hot water steep over coarsely ground coffee for 3-4 minutes before pressing down the filter and serving. It doesn’t get more simple than that. 

This French Press has become the go to for anybody who wants a beautiful freshly brewed coffee at home or office.

 This one by Timemore Co. has made the design brilliantly sleek!

It just gets Darker here now. A few degrees darker than Vienna profile.
